Description: A unique alphanumeric identifier assigned to each registered system user for authentication authorization and audit trail purposes. This identifier serves as the primary key in the user management system and is used across all application modules to track user actions enforce access controls and maintain data security compliance.
Business Logic: Must be unique across all users; cannot be null or empty; length between 6 and 50 characters; cannot be changed after creation; must persist even after user account deactivation for audit history; alphanumeric and special characters (@.-_) only

Description: The elapsed time in minutes between user login and logout (or timeout) measuring how long a user maintains an active authenticated session. This metric is critical for analyzing user engagement patterns optimizing session timeout policies and identifying potential security anomalies from abnormally long sessions.
Business Logic: Must be greater than 0; maximum session duration is 480 minutes (8 hours); sessions exceeding 30 minutes of inactivity are automatically terminated; duration calculated only for successfully authenticated sessions; concurrent sessions from same user are tracked separately

Description: The percentage of time the application system is fully operational and accessible to users over a defined measurement period calculated as total available time divided by total time excluding scheduled maintenance windows. This metric is a key Service Level Agreement (SLA) indicator measuring system reliability and is used to assess infrastructure performance.
Business Logic: Must be between 0 and 100; calculated hourly daily and monthly; excludes planned maintenance windows documented in change management system; SLA target is 99.9% monthly; values below 99.5% trigger incident investigation; includes only production environment downtime

Description: The time in milliseconds elapsed between receiving an API request and sending the complete response measuring the performance and efficiency of API endpoints. This metric is monitored to ensure optimal user experience identify performance bottlenecks and maintain service level objectives for application responsiveness.
Business Logic: Must be greater than 0; target response time is under 200ms for 95th percentile; responses exceeding 2000ms (2 seconds) trigger performance alerts; measured at application layer excluding network latency; calculated only for successful HTTP 200 responses; aggregated by endpoint and time period

Description: The percentage of failed requests or transactions relative to total requests over a specified time period used to measure system stability and data quality. This metric helps identify system issues data validation problems and integration failures requiring immediate attention.
Business Logic: Must be greater than or equal to 0; target is below 1.0% for production systems; values above 5% trigger critical alerts; calculated hourly and daily; includes HTTP 4xx and 5xx errors; excludes intentional validation rejections; tracked by endpoint and error type

Description: The number of active concurrent connections to the database server at a given point in time measuring database resource utilization and application load. This metric is monitored to prevent connection pool exhaustion and ensure optimal database performance.
Business Logic: Must be non-negative; cannot exceed maximum connection pool size; monitored in real-time; values approaching maximum trigger scaling actions; connections should be properly released after use; idle connections beyond timeout are automatically closed; tracked by application and database instance

Description: The total count of registered users with unique user identifiers in the system used to monitor user base growth track licensing requirements and analyze system capacity planning needs. This metric distinguishes between active and inactive users for different reporting purposes.
Business Logic: Must be greater than or equal to 0; calculated from unique user identifiers only; updated in real-time or batch; includes both active and inactive users unless specified; used for license compliance and capacity planning; excludes deleted or archived users

Description: The total number of API requests received by the system within a specified time period used to measure system usage monitor capacity and identify traffic patterns. This volume metric is essential for capacity planning performance analysis and billing in usage-based models.
Business Logic: Must be non-negative; aggregated by time period (hour day month); tracked per endpoint and API version; used for capacity planning and billing; includes successful failed and cached requests; excludes requests blocked by rate limiting; monitored for unusual spikes indicating attacks

Description: The percentage of requests successfully served from cache versus total requests measuring cache effectiveness and system performance optimization. A higher ratio indicates better cache utilization reducing database load and improving response times.
Business Logic: Must be between 0 and 1; target is above 0.80 for frequently accessed data; calculated over rolling time windows; lower ratios trigger cache optimization reviews; tracked by cache layer and data type; excludes cache misses due to first-time requests

Description: The time in seconds required to process and transform data from ingestion to completion used to measure ETL performance batch job efficiency and data pipeline throughput. This metric identifies bottlenecks and ensures data is available within required timeframes for business operations.
Business Logic: Must be greater than 0; compared against SLA targets for each job; values exceeding thresholds trigger alerts; tracked per job type and data volume; includes validation transformation and loading time; used for capacity planning and optimization; measured from job start to completion

Description: The mean time in milliseconds required to process and respond to user requests aggregated across all endpoints or specific services. This metric provides an overall view of system responsiveness and user experience quality.
Synonyms: Mean Response Time|Average Latency|Mean Request Duration
Business Logic: Must be greater than 0; calculated as arithmetic mean across successful requests; target varies by endpoint type (100-500ms typical); excludes outliers beyond 99th percentile; tracked hourly and daily; lower values indicate better performance; used for SLA compliance reporting

Description: The amount of storage space in gigabytes currently consumed by the application database logs and temporary files. This metric is monitored to prevent storage exhaustion ensure adequate capacity and trigger cleanup or scaling actions when thresholds are approached.
Business Logic: Must be non-negative; cannot exceed total allocated storage; monitored continuously; alerts triggered at 80% capacity; includes database files log files and temporary storage; excludes archived data; automatic cleanup policies applied for temporary files; tracked by volume and partition

Description: The percentage of available RAM currently being utilized by the application processes measuring memory consumption and potential resource constraints. This metric helps identify memory leaks prevent out-of-memory errors and optimize resource allocation.
Business Logic: Must be between 0 and 100; target is below 80% for healthy operation; values above 90% trigger scaling or optimization actions; calculated from allocated vs used memory; includes application heap and non-heap memory; monitored in real-time; sustained high values indicate potential memory leaks

Description: The percentage of CPU processing capacity currently being utilized by application processes measuring computational load and system performance. This metric indicates processing efficiency resource contention and the need for horizontal or vertical scaling.
Business Logic: Must be between 0 and 100; target is below 70% for normal operations; values above 85% trigger performance investigations; calculated across all cores or per core; monitored in real-time; sustained high values trigger auto-scaling; includes user and system CPU time; excludes idle time
